questions.enonce_markdown: Find the value of $x$ for which $4^x + 4(2^x) = 12$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Write $4^x = (2^x)^2$ and let $u = 2^x$ (so $u > 0$):
$$u^2 + 4u - 12 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; (u + 6)(u - 2) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; u = -6 \ \text{ or } \ u = 2.$$
$u = -6$ is rejected because $2^x > 0$ for all real $x$. So $2^x = 2$, giving $x = 1$.

Check: $4^1 + 4(2^1) = 4 + 8 = 12$.
$$\boxed{x = 1}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
The determinant of a matrix $\mathbf{M}$ is $45$, where
$$\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & \alpha - 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$
Show that $\alpha = 2$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Expand the determinant along the third row (which contains a zero):
$$\det\mathbf{M} = 1\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ \alpha - 1 & 6 \end{vmatrix} - 4\begin{vmatrix} \alpha & 5 \\ 4 & 6 \end{vmatrix} + 0 = \big(18 - 5(\alpha - 1)\big) - 4\big(6\alpha - 20\big)$$
$$= 23 - 5\alpha - 24\alpha + 80 = 103 - 29\alpha.$$
Given $\det\mathbf{M} = 45$: $103 - 29\alpha = 45 \Rightarrow 29\alpha = 58$.
$$\boxed{\alpha = 2}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & \alpha - 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ has determinant $45$ (so $\alpha = 2$), find $\mathbf{M}^{-1}$, the inverse of matrix $\mathbf{M}$. Hence, solve the system of equations
$$2x + 3y + 5z = 30, \qquad 4x + y + 6z = 27, \qquad x + 4y = 45.$$ (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $\alpha = 2$: $\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 4 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$, $\det\mathbf{M} = 45$.

**Cofactors** $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i + j}M_{ij}$:
$$C_{11} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -24,\quad C_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 6,\quad C_{13} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 15,$$
$$C_{21} = -\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 20,\quad C_{22} = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = -5,\quad C_{23} = -\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = -5,$$
$$C_{31} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 13,\quad C_{32} = -\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 8,\quad C_{33} = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -10.$$
(Check of the determinant along the first row: $2(-24) + 3(6) + 5(15) = -48 + 18 + 75 = 45$.)

The adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix, and $\mathbf{M}^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\det\mathbf{M}}\,\mathrm{adj}\,\mathbf{M}$:
$$\boxed{\mathbf{M}^{-1} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} -24 & 20 & 13 \\ 6 & -5 & 8 \\ 15 & -5 & -10 \end{pmatrix}}$$

**The system.** In matrix form the three equations are $\mathbf{M}\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 30 \\ 27 \\ 45 \end{pmatrix}$, hence
$$\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{M}^{-1}\begin{pmatrix} 30 \\ 27 \\ 45 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} -720 + 540 + 585 \\ 180 - 135 + 360 \\ 450 - 135 - 450 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{45}\begin{pmatrix} 405 \\ 405 \\ -135 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ 9 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}.$$
$$\boxed{x = 9, \quad y = 9, \quad z = -3}$$
Check: $2(9) + 3(9) + 5(-3) = 30$; $4(9) + 9 + 6(-3) = 27$; $9 + 4(9) = 45$.
